full_judgment:
2. In the instant suit for confirmation of possession after establishment of the plaintiffs dar rayti right to suit land, it is the common case of both the parties that there was a dar rayati in respect of 4 Kanis, 1½ gondas land with an annual jama of Tk. 25/6/3 held by Fazu Mia and others, predecessors of the defendants under the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Both sides admit that this dar rayati was created in 1313 B.S. by the Kabuliyat Ext. 1. The disputed land, namely, C.S. plot Nos.3217, 3218, 3219 and 3291 of Khatian No.230 of Mouza Yarpur, is part of this dar rayati. It is also the common case of the parties that out of this dar rayati land of 4 kanis and 1.5 gondas, the plaintiffs purchased 3 kanis, 7 gondas and 1 kag land by different kabalas, Ext.2 series and there remained 14 gondas 2 kag with the defendants. A seperate jama of Tk. 3/14/6 was creased by a fresh Kabuliyat Ext. 1(a) executed by the defendants on the 8th Sraban, 1326 B.S. The fresh Kabuliyat Ext. 1(a) covers not only the disputed plots but also some other plots, namely, C.S. plot Nos. 3272, 3284, 3287, 3292, 3295 and 3296. The plaintiffs claim that the disputed land is part of their purchased land which the defendants contend that it is part of their subsequent Kabuliat Ext. 1(a). The plaintiffs claim that they are in possession of the 4 disputed plots and the defendants also claim so. 

 4. The learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Sadar Noakhali, by his judgment and decree dated 12.8.59, decreed T.S. No. 57 of 1954, A local investigation was made to ascertain whether the disputed plots Nos.3217-19 and 3291 were covered by the kabalas of the plaintiff. After relayment the Pleadar Commissioner reported that the disputed land is covered by the kabala of the plaintiffs Ext.2 dated 27th Bhadra, 1321 B.S. This is the earliest Kabala of the plaintiffs. This was taken in the benami of one Kerammat Ali who executed a nadabi patra Ext.3 on the 28th Asar, 1326 B.S.C.S. operation followed soon after the kabala of the plaintiffs Ext.2 and shortly before the kabuliyat of the defendants. C.S. Khatain Ext.4 shows that the disputed plots together with other plots were recorded in the possession of the plaintiffs. The trial court held that the plaintiffs Kabaliat Ext.2, the C.S. Khatian Ext.4, the nadabi patra Ext.3 and the report of the Pleader Commissioner proved that the disputed land belonged to the plaintiffs. The only documentary evidence of the defendant is the Kabuliat Ext. 1(a). On possession, the trial Court held that it finds nothing to disbelieve 7 P.Ws. owners of neighbouring land. 5 witnesses examined by the defence had worked as badlas of the defendants were not impressive and such witnesses were not difficult to procure at any time. The trial Court was unable to place any reliance upon them. The dakhilas filed by the defendants are not related to the suit land. On the finding that the disputed plots are the kabla and of the plaintiffs and not part of the defendants fresh kabuliat Ext. 1(a), the trail court decreed the suit.
